requirement:
The Rust outline exposes the following items beneath its file root:

| Construct | Kind | Name |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Functions, methods, and function signatures | `fn` | Declared name |
| Structs, enums, unions, and traits | `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait` | Declared name |
| Implementations | `impl` | Written self type and optional trait path |
| Modules | `mod` | Declared name |
| Macro definitions | `macro` | Declared name |
| Macro invocations in item position | `macro` | Anonymous |
| Constants and statics | `const`, `static` | Declared name |
| Type aliases and associated types | `type` | Declared name |
| Foreign blocks | `extern` | ABI string, or `Rust` when absent |
| Extern-crate declarations | `extern-crate` | Declared name |
| Imports | `use` | Anonymous |

An implementation of `Trait` for `Thing` uses `impl[Thing/Trait]`;
an inherent implementation uses `impl[Thing]`. Nesting follows source
containment within the file. Outer attributes and outer documentation comments
attach to the following item; inner documentation comments belong to their
containing item or file root.

Item selectors, percent encoding, anonymous identities, and duplicate-name
suffixes follow {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.items` has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. Its clauses describe only what the Rust outline shows. They don't prescribe how to build it.

- The construct, kind and name table says the outline "exposes the following items beneath its file root". An implementation could produce the same items with a different parser, a hand-written scanner, or a different internal representation. Observable behavior would stay the same, so the choice of approach is discretionary.
- The clause "An implementation of `Trait` for `Thing` uses `impl[Thing/Trait]`; an inherent implementation uses `impl[Thing]`" fixes the selector text. That is output, not a code structure. Any code that yields these selectors satisfies it.
- The clauses "Nesting follows source containment within the file" and "Outer attributes and outer documentation comments attach to the following item; inner documentation comments belong to their containing item or file root" are also observable outline properties. No library, type, signature or delegation is named.
- The last clause delegates selector grammar, percent encoding, anonymous identities and duplicate-name suffixes to `requirements.references.outline_selectors`. That requirement only says Habeas uses the TBV selector grammar. It is cited as context and gives no extra structural obligation here.

The review roots are empty and `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.items` has no Implements edges. Since every clause is behavioral, no root is missing. The behavior itself is left to the test-adequacy criterion.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.items`.

**Kinds and names**
- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` checks selectors and resolution for these constructs:
  - fn: free functions, methods, trait signatures (`trait[Trait]/fn[read]`) and foreign fns (`extern[C]/fn[puts]`).
  - struct, union, enum and trait.
  - mod, both inline and `mod[external]`.
  - macro definitions (`macro[make]`).
  - const and static.
  - type aliases and trait associated types (`type[Alias]`, `trait[Trait]/type[Item]`).
  - extern blocks, with ABI `C` and with `Rust` when the ABI is absent.
  - extern-crate (`extern-crate[core]`).
- Impl naming is covered for both forms: `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`.
  - `[u8; 4]` self types are percent-encoded.
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` in `tests/outline_content.rs` checks a qualified trait path, `impl[Thing/core::fmt::Display]`.
  - `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` checks generics, `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
  - `rust_name_spans_highlight_spelling_in_the_original_source` checks the same generic selector and `extern[Rust]` for `unsafe extern {}`.

**Anonymous items**
- `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` and `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` check `use@…` selectors.
- The second test also checks item-position `macro@<12 hex>` selectors at file level, in an impl and in a mod. It asserts that macros inside a function body (expression macros) produce no nodes.

**Nesting**
- Nested selectors are asserted for mod, impl, trait, extern and fn-in-fn. The `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` test also checks the ordered item list with kinds.

**Attributes and documentation**
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` asserts that the fn's span and text start at the outer `///` doc comment and include `#[inline]`.
- `comment_runs_belong_to_the_next_node_or_their_container` and `file_level_inner_doc_comments_and_unmapped_code_belong_to_the_root` check inner docs.
  - Inner doc comments (`//!` and `/*! */`) belong to the file root or to their containing mod.
  - Comments before an item belong to that item.

**Selector grammar**
- Percent encoding, anonymous identities and duplicate suffixes are delegated to the cited `requirements.references.outline_selectors`. The tests also exercise them: `#1`/`#2` for duplicates, and identity hashes that stay stable when other items are inserted or changed.

All of these tests carry `{test}` markers for the subject. I found no unasserted obligation and no marking gap.
